_comment: Sample responses from Hacker News API - https://hacker-news.firebaseio.com/v0/

topstories_endpoint._description: Returns up to 500 top story IDs

response.title: Show HN: I built a tool to analyze datasets

item_endpoint_comment._description: A comment item - note: comments can have nested kids (child comments)

response.text: This is really impressive! I've been looking for something like this. How does it handle missing values?
Thanks! It uses multiple imputation strategies depending on the data type.

item_types.story: A top-level submission with url or text
item_types.comment: A comment on a story or another comment

item_fields.deleted: true if the item is deleted (boolean)
item_fields.type: The type of item: job, story, comment, poll, or pollopt
item_fields.by: The username of the item's author
item_fields.time: Creation date of the item, Unix timestamp
item_fields.text: The comment, story or poll text (HTML)
item_fields.dead: true if the item is dead (boolean)
item_fields.parent: The comment's parent: either another comment or the story
item_fields.kids: The ids of the item's comments, in ranked display order (array)
item_fields.score: The story's score, or the votes for a pollopt
item_fields.title: The title of the story, poll or job
item_fields.parts: A list of related pollopts, in display order
item_fields.descendants: Total comment count for stories and polls

notes.rate_limits: No official rate limit, but be respectful (1-2 requests/second recommended)
notes.recursive_fetching: To get all comments, recursively fetch items from the 'kids' array
notes.deleted_items: Some items may be deleted - handle gracefully
notes.dead_items: Some items may be 'dead' (flagged/killed) - still accessible but marked
